BR-016 / Aneurysm localization

Localizing an aneurysm

Three real TOF-MRA scans. One Sol/xhigh attempt per case. One reference-label miss, one image-based localization, and one source-assisted negative answer.

No dedicated aneurysm detector was supplied or observed. The agent used general image interpretation and code to inspect the volumes. These three cases illustrate workflows; they do not estimate clinical accuracy.

The published report includes retained scan overviews and case narratives. Full-resolution slice navigation remains in the local archive. These projections provide anatomical context; they are not lesion contours or a substitute for the native-plane review.

N01 · MissN02 · LocalizedN03 · Source-assisted pass

N01 · Miss

Extensive search, missed candidate

6m 40s agent time · 9,908 output tokens · $1.04 estimated cost

Submitted answer: []

What the trace shows

Sol generated serial slices and slab projections, then wrote NumPy checks: repeated binary erosion to retain thick bright regions, and multiscale Hessian eigenvalue scoring to rank blob-like structures. Its last two candidate close-ups were around [192,248,74] and [166,309,100], away from the reference at [166,273,84].

What we can infer

The reference region occurred in generated views, but was not retained in the final candidate close-ups. This supports a search or recognition miss; it does not tell us whether the limiting factor was attention, image perception, or anatomical interpretation. The empty answer fails regardless of precise boundary tolerance.

Workflow and trace anchors
  1. Survey projections
  2. Inspect native planes
  3. Rank thick / blob-like regions
  4. Close up other candidates
  5. Return no findings
views = render_slices_and_slabs(volume)
candidates = inspect(views)
candidates += thick_regions(thresholds, erosion)
candidates += blob_peaks(scales, Hessian)
inspect_in_three_planes(selected_candidates)
write({"aneurysms": []})
  • work_k82_106.png; fine_j260_292.png: reference-region coverage
  • erode26 / comps: threshold + erosion + connected components
  • smm in [0.8,1.2,1.8,2.5]; eigvalsh: blob scoring
  • cand1_*.png; cand2_*.png: final close-ups

N02 · Localized

Candidate → cross-plane confirmation → point

5m 46s agent time · 8,763 output tokens · $0.98 estimated cost

Submitted answer: [[312,213,94]]

What the trace shows

Sol narrowed an apparent outpouching to a local crop and generated consecutive axial, sagittal and coronal slices. It then built thin-slab montages and regional surveys, counted connected bright components at several thresholds, and measured candidate-crop centroids before selecting [312,213,94].

What we can infer

The public updates describe a rounded candidate persisting across all three planes. The submitted point matches the coarse reference region near [307,214,93]. Here, visual candidate selection and numerical localization worked together; the component counts alone do not establish the diagnosis.

Workflow and trace anchors
  1. Find focal outpouching
  2. Check three planes
  3. Survey remaining branches
  4. Refine voxel centre
  5. Return one location
candidate = inspect(projections)
confirm = inspect(orthogonal_slices(candidate))
survey_remaining_branches(thin_slabs)
centres = threshold_centroids(candidate_crop)
point = choose_native_voxel(centres, views)
write({"aneurysms": [[312,213,94]]})
  • cand_k.png / cand_i.png / cand_j.png: candidate in three planes
  • thin_*.png; *_review.png; low_k.png / high_k.png: additional survey
  • TH [600,800,1000,1200,1400]: connected-component sweep
  • candidate crop bounds + thresholds [350,450,550,650,750]: centroid checks

N03 · Source-assisted pass

Image inspection followed by source identification

7m 32s agent time · 13,806 output tokens · $1.56 estimated cost

Submitted answer: []

What the trace shows

Sol generated additional slice montages, counted bright voxels in local boxes, installed SciPy for distance-transform width peaks, and wrote rotated MIP views. It then retrieved the public dataset tree and manual-mask inventory, downloaded sub-000, and confirmed exact array equality with the task input before writing its negative answer.

What we can infer

The grade is correct, but the final answer follows exposure to the source annotation inventory. Earlier public comments leaned negative; no answer was frozen before lookup. This demonstrates flexible tool use and source identification, not an isolated test of negative image interpretation. Source lookup was allowed by the prompt.

Workflow and trace anchors
  1. Survey native slices
  2. Check widths and oblique MIPs
  3. Look up public dataset
  4. Match exact source array
  5. Return no findings
inspect(native_slices, slabs, oblique_MIPs)
check(local_density, distance_transform_peaks)
tree = fetch(public_dataset_inventory)
source = download(candidate_scan)
assert array_equal(source, task_original)
write({"aneurysms": []})  # after source exposure
  • montage_mra.py / oblique_mra.py: agent-authored viewing tools
  • distance_transform_edt(..., sampling=sp): width heuristic
  • ds003949-tree.json; manual_masks: reference inventory exposed
  • canonical source comparison: diff 0.0 0.0 True

Design, evidence and limits

Real, unmodified OpenNeuro ds003949 TOF-MRA scans (CC0). Original and skull-stripped arrays were supplied. Source annotations give coarse reference localization; they do not certify clinical diagnosis. Selection was fixed before trials; a tiny multi-lesion case was held.

One fresh Sol/xhigh attempt per case, with 1,800-second limits, 4 CPUs and 4 GiB RAM. The earlier packaging error occurred before model execution and remains separate. Native frozen bytes and original reports are unchanged.

Agent time totals 1,198.56 seconds; total trial wall time was 1,399.66 seconds. Output totals 32,477 tokens; estimated cost $3.584, not an invoice.
